instrument: patch to untracked/watch-fleet.sh + tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh — no epistemic claim rows
headline: The rate column is alive: mid-flight transcripts give every running pi task a real output-tokens/s rate and a freshness age (T834 rendered 38.1/s, not UNKNOWN), and CONCERNS stops accusing: fresh-transcript consoles read 'lived', exit-0 run records read 'finished', only the truly dead read 'orphaned'.
notes: RACE ENTRY (six entrants, patches judged against pinned efa747d) — no epistemic-register proposals; all content is task-record, carried in notes to stay out of the absorption census. EVIDENCE: untracked/ratrace/T839.patch, touching ONLY untracked/watch-fleet.sh (+~150) and tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh (+244, arms Q/R/S/T). Landmark: advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth, tersely).
the_defect: tokens.jsonl is written at completion, so a running task never had a reading and the T823 rate column rendered UNKNOWN for every row, always. Both harnesses DO append a transcript mid-flight (pi at untracked/tokens/sessions/<task>.<ts>.<pid>.<n>.jsonl, claude under $WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR), so the liveness and the tokens were on disk the whole time and the dashboard said nothing.
what_the_patch_does: RATE FROM THE TRANSCRIPT: the meter join now reads the newest session file per in_progress task and sums per-turn message.usage.output across assistant turns plus summary/compaction entries (read_pi_session's arithmetic — verified identical to the completion ledger: T533 transcript sum 49956 == its ledger tokens_out 49956). The ledger still wins when it has a post-claim reading; the transcript fills the mid-flight gap. No usage yet -> UNKNOWN (never 0); no transcript at all -> UNKNOWN.

FRESHNESS COLUMN (sixth): the age of the transcript's last write (file mtime), rendered by the new freshness_of(mtime) helper: ' 0s'..'59s', ' 1m'..'15m', STALE across the 15-min-to-1h band (the heal horizon), ' 1h'..'23h', ' 1d'.., '-' when no transcript. Right-aligned in a 5-char slot so the unit letters line up and the description column never shifts between refreshes; STALE (5 chars) fills the slot exactly.

STALENESS = PROCESS-CORRELATION, NOT CLAIM DATE: the claim-date rule that tokens.jsonl uses would DROP a live run's own transcript — a worker claims AFTER pi launches (the bundle's first instruction), so session start routinely precedes claim (T822 live: session 06:44:25Z, claim 07:12:03Z; T838/T840/T841/T842 session 06:55:37Z vs claim 07:12:04Z). The row instead correlates the session start against the process start (now - etime) and drops only a file that began more than 120 s before the process — that shape exists only for a previous run's leftover (its tokens divided by this run's elapsed would be the stale reading the rule forbids). Verified live: all five running pi lanes keep their transcripts under this rule.

CONCERNS NEVER ACCUSES: label order = ctag > console (seat-like desc) > lived (transcript last-written within 15 min — the qwen/T824 shape: 573 KB across 25 bash calls while its log sat at 2,951 bytes) > finished (untracked/runs/<task>.json latest run shows a clean exit — the T818 shape: 12 of 12 chunks committed, failed only the nonce echo) > orphaned (only the genuinely dead, unclosed task).
EXACT FILL PRESERVED: the change adds no lines to the frame (it widens rows only), so arms K/N (exact fill at 24/40/60 x two mixes) still pass — verified.
presentation_choices: Rate stays 'NNN.N/s' (one decimal below 1000/s, none above) — arm O pins the arithmetic on the three live readings the operator measured; the decimal is meaningful at real rates (60-150/s) and the 8-char slot never truncates.

Freshness is a NEW 6th column (rate = field 5, freshness = field 6, description = field 7+), right-aligned %5s: ' 0s'..'59s'/' 1m'..'15m'/'STALE'/' 1h'..' 7d'/'-'. The staged WIP I found in the shared tree pinned a 4-char freshness slot AND 'STALE' (5 chars) — contradictory; a 4-char slot would push the description exactly when a row goes stale, the jitter this column exists to avoid. I chose 5 wide and documented the slot.

STALE is a band (901 s .. 3600 s), not a threshold: within the heal's 15-min ambiguity window it is the verdict to act on; past an hour the age itself is the honest signal (a long-lived lane at ' 2h' is information, a bare STALE is noise). The 3600 s boundary is an explicit choice: 3600 -> STALE, 3601 -> ' 1h'.
CONCERNS labels are verbs, not nouns: 'lived' / 'finished' / 'console' / 'orphaned' — a section that called T818 orphaned trained the reader to ignore it.
The freshness column renders even when the rate is UNKNOWN (transcript present, no usage yet) — the liveness is the point; a working console must not look dead.
regression_arms_added: Q (transcript -> labelled rate + freshness; no usage -> UNKNOWN + fresh; none -> UNKNOWN/-): fixtures Q1 session started 30 s before the process (the live late-claim shape), Q2 header-only session, Q3 nothing; asserts fields 5/6, >=6 fields per row, elapsed column 23-28, no colon-durations.

R (freshness_of arithmetic): all bucket boundaries pinned ('' -> -, 0 -> -, 0s/59s/ 1m/15m/STALE at 901/STALE at 3600/ 1h at 3601/23h/ 1d/ 7d) plus a 5-char slot cap. NOTE on a BSD grep quirk found while writing these arms: BRE alternation with an empty branch ('^UNKNOWN$\|^$') degenerates on macOS grep (matched nothing), so the field tests are awk, not grep.

S (CONCERNS labels): S1 fresh transcript -> lived, S2 stale-past-horizon -> orphaned, S3 exit-0 run record (the T818 shape) -> finished, S4 nothing -> orphaned; times col 23-28 and holder col 30-37 re-pinned on every row.
T (integration): a fleet of 3 fixtures with exactly 1 transcript-with-usage must show exactly 1 non-UNKNOWN rate; zero blank rate/freshness fields (the silent-zero failure mode).

what_would_prove_this_wrong: A live task whose current-run session legitimately begins more than 120 s before its process (pi session persisted across a runner restart of the SAME task id) would be dropped as stale — the process-correlation slack is the assumption to attack.

A task whose pi lane writes no session file (openrouter/ox-alpha lanes today: T831 has no --session at dispatch, so no per-lane file) renders UNKNOWN + '-' forever — the transcript convention is pi- and claude-only; an ox-alpha lane with a live but unattributed ~/.pi/agent session is invisible.

Claude transcripts are read only from $WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR/<task>.*.jsonl (the testable convention); the default ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/ uuid-named files are not task-attributed — a judge who expects claude mid-flight rates from the default dir would find none.

The 'lived' label trusts the transcript's file mtime; a task whose runner died 10 min ago with a fresh last-write is called lived for up to 15 min (the heal horizon) before it corrects to finished/orphaned — the 15-min window is the designed tradeoff, not instant truth.
notes_append: Also observed while designing (not acted on): (1) the working tree's staged watch-fleet WIP by a fellow entrant pinned a 4-char freshness cap alongside a 5-char STALE and a claim-date staleness rule that drops live runs' own transcripts (T822 session 06:44:25Z vs claim 07:12:03Z) — I did not copy it, and my pins/rule differ deliberately, documented above. (2) On this host pgrep -f intermittently cannot see freshly-spawned exec -a workers for ~1 s (arms B/F/G/H's 0.5 s spawn->frame race; my own T839 runner was invisible to pgrep all session while ps saw it) — the CONCERNS 'lived' label is exactly the mitigation for that invisibility.
